name: Field Condition
description: The condition of the field, such as the presence of obstacles or uneven terrain, can significantly affect travel time. Poor conditions can lead to delays and increased travel time.

name: Obstacles
description: Presence of obstacles such as fallen branches, crops, or other debris can slow down the robot and increase travel time. Path 1 might have more obstacles due to its proximity to the edge of the field.

name: Terrain
description: The type of terrain, such as hard-packed soil versus soft soil, can affect the robot's speed. Uneven or soft terrain can slow the robot down.

name: Weather Conditions
description: Rain, wind, or other weather conditions can affect the robot's travel time. For example, heavy rain can turn Path 2 into a muddy path, reducing speed.

name: Crop Stage
description: The stage of crop growth can affect the path's condition. During harvesting or when crops are tall, Path 2 might be more obstructed, increasing travel time.

name: Sunlight
description: Lighting conditions can affect the visibility for the robot's cameras, potentially causing delays. Path 2 might be more shaded, leading to poorer visibility.

name: Traffic
description: The presence of other robots or vehicles in the field can delay the robot. Path 1 might be more congested if it is used by more robots.

name: Battery Level
description: The battery level of the robot can affect its speed. A low battery might reduce its speed, affecting travel time, especially on longer Path 1.

name: Maintenance
description: The overall maintenance state of the robot can affect its performance. Older or poorly maintained robots might experience mechanical issues, leading to increased travel time.

name: Sensor Calibration
description: The calibration of the robot's sensors can affect its ability to navigate correctly. Misaligned cameras or sensors can cause the robot to take longer to make decisions.

name: Speed Setting
description: The speed setting of the robot can be adjusted based on the current conditions. If the speed is set too low, it can increase travel time.

name: Software Performance
description: The performance of the robot's software can affect its decision-making speed. If the software is slow, the robot might take longer to make route decisions.

name: Noise
description: Environmental noise can affect the robot's sensors, particularly if the cameras rely on visual cues. High noise levels can reduce visibility and increase travel time.

name: Temperature
description: Extreme temperatures can affect the robot's hardware, potentially causing delays if the temperature is too high or too low for optimal operation.

name: Signal Strength
description: The strength of the communication signal between the robot and the controller can affect the robot's ability to receive and process instructions. Weak signals can cause delays.
